Boundary: Household, caregiver membership and tenant-scope rules are implemented and host-tested. The reference backend still uses development identity/in-memory runtime state for the connected lab; production OIDC/session handling and transactional persistent deployment remain outside this evidence.
Acceptance experiment: Create a valid household, repeat the same creation request, try a missing-consent draft, assign the same primary and backup, and attempt cross-house access. Check both returned errors and stored membership records.

Boundary: Consent withdrawal and internal privacy gating are host-tested. The normal household Settings UI no longer exposes a Privacy ON/OFF toggle; explicit consent withdrawal may still force the internal privacy state. Real sensor-side collection stop, retention/deletion and field privacy behavior require target integration.
Acceptance experiment: During an active routine, withdraw consent and send passive events before and after application acknowledgement. Confirm visible privacy state, no false absence incident and no resumption without a deliberate new state transition.

Boundary: Onboarding validation, capability checks and installation-gate semantics are host-tested. Actual board identity, GPIO capability, RF/input placement and installed-home verification remain a HIL/field gate.
Acceptance experiment: Reject duplicate node IDs and wrong-board configuration. Walk each intended path, disconnect one sensor, test every resident button and perform a real notification drill before enabling unattended alerts.

Boundary: Morning-routine policy plus quiet hours, door-left-open timeout and daytime inactivity settings are versioned per household through the web/API/config path and applied to the hardware-independent rule configuration. Persistent target-side atomic application still requires real hub storage/integration.
Acceptance experiment: Apply an increasing version, reject an older one, simulate a time-zone boundary and a mid-window update, and inspect desired versus applied state. Do not mark the schedule active just because the API accepted it.

Browser/manual: Timeline presentation covered by manual plan
Boundary: Generic motion/door events are consumed independently of GPIO and are preserved with location/time in the connected simulator. Real PIR/reed debounce, placement, electrical behavior and radio delivery remain physical acceptance items.
Acceptance experiment: Replay allowed/disallowed locations, test events, out-of-window events and duplicate event IDs. Check household wording and separate coverage. A new replay test must expose duplicate evidence IDs rather than assuming journal deduplication protects the reducer.

Browser/manual: Manual visual check: green + elapsed age
Boundary: I am OK is a distinct positive self-check-in with age and chronology. It does not erase an unresolved Call Family incident. Physical button debounce, reachability and the <500 ms local-feedback target require real hardware/usability measurement.
Acceptance experiment: Test press, bounce, held button, WAN outage and reboot between save and send. Measure the 500 ms local confirmation target on hardware. Verify that a caregiver acknowledgement cannot masquerade as resident OK.

Boundary: Call Family creates a durable host incident, primary/backup routes and offline replay while remaining independent of later motion or I am OK. Real push/SMS/voice delivery and phone receipt are not claimed.
Acceptance experiment: Send the same request twice and verify one incident and one job per recipient/stage. Exercise WAN loss, reboot, provider rejection and a caregiver acknowledgement that cancels pending backup routing.

Boundary: The C++ rule engine drives missing-morning behavior through the connected simulator; later activity remains visible while the earlier concern remains in history. Continuous historical coverage is still not proven by the current lease model (G03).
Acceptance experiment: Run covered quiet, evidence present, node missing, clock invalid, privacy, away, visitor and repeated-deadline cases. Restart mid-window and confirm persisted eligibility and duplicate suppression before accepting the hardware implementation.

Boundary: Door open/close is explicit, quiet-hours opening is classified as unexpected, configurable door-left-open timing generates a concern, and later close records duration/resolution. These decisions now come from the C++ RulesCore. Real reed mounting/wiring and field timing remain pending.
Acceptance experiment: Test bounce, initial open state, repeat delivery, quiet policy off, policy boundary and test-tagged data. Inspect the notice label for direction or identity claims.

Boundary: ACTIVE/AWAY/PAUSED/VISITOR suppression semantics are covered by the functional catalog. Production authorization, durable config application and target-side controls still require deployment integration.
Acceptance experiment: Change each mode before, during and after a window; repeat an old command and reboot. Confirm that collection policy, absence eligibility and displayed mode agree.

Boundary: The simulator/PWA projection shows exact activity, chronology, unresolved incidents, device health/location and availability separately. JavaScript and functional tests pass. Actual browser automation was not recorded as passed because Playwright is not installed; the generated manual browser plan is the current visual gate.
Acceptance experiment: Load fresh, stale, never-seen and disconnected snapshots; change phone time; try H2 credentials for H1; verify that labels remain understandable on a small mobile screen.

Boundary: Claim, acknowledge and resolve lifecycle plus ownership conflict behavior are host-tested. Action-specific authorization and transactional compare-and-set for production concurrency remain G08.
Acceptance experiment: Race two claims, expire a lease, try cross-house access, repeat acknowledgement and resolve a closed incident. Verify authorised action permissions and notification cancellation in a transaction-level test.

Browser/manual: Delivery visibility covered in host UI
Boundary: Primary/backup routing, provider acceptance state and human acknowledgement are represented separately and regression-tested. A real delivery worker, retry leases and provider ambiguity handling remain G10.
Acceptance experiment: Use a fake provider that accepts, rejects and times out. Crash a worker after sending but before saving the result. Verify idempotency and clear uncertain-delivery status instead of claiming guaranteed exactly-once notification.

End to end: Backend component PASS; full connected summary pending
Browser/manual: Summary UI not a completed release gate
Boundary: The host summary helper is opt-in/idempotent and coverage-aware, but it still scans retained home activity without complete local-date filtering and direct consent enforcement. Same-day policy-version behavior remains G07.
Acceptance experiment: Test no opt-in, no consent, events only from yesterday, partial coverage, repeated scheduling and policy change on the same date. Decide whether a policy revision should update or resend before implementing production routing.

Boundary: The reference defines 60 s heartbeat / 190 s offline semantics and exposes active/degraded/offline devices with locations plus simulated fault codes. Real battery calibration, RSSI distributions, thermal telemetry and missed-heartbeat behavior require HIL.
Acceptance experiment: Test never-seen, fresh, expired, explicit sensor fault and uncalibrated voltage. Measure battery impact and packet loss before freezing heartbeat intervals.

Boundary: A typed node-to-hub message/ACK contract now defines source/session/sequence identity, sensor/event type, time, battery, RSSI, durable ACK, retry and duplicate semantics. Real ESP-NOW encoding/authentication/channel recovery remain G09; retained-event refill remains G05.
Acceptance experiment: Inject lost packet, lost ACK, duplicate packet, reordered packet, peer mismatch and receiver-full conditions. Examine both event counts and side effects such as evidence IDs and notification jobs.

Boundary: WAN loss, local progression, replay and delayed/backfilled behavior are covered in connected tests. The runtime store is still in memory and real router power, flash persistence and ESP-NOW coexistence remain physical/deployment work.
Acceptance experiment: Separate WAN cut, router off, hub reboot and node off. Check the correct status for each, and verify replay without erasing the observation gap.

Boundary: Host read models separate activity evidence, node/hub freshness, WAN/backend reachability and human workflow state. Production broker/stream refresh, phone reachability and durable stale-state recovery remain deployment items.
Acceptance experiment: Break one boundary at a time and verify that the other statuses remain correct. Confirm that broker retained online state is not used as the sole liveness proof.

Boundary: A concrete relational model and migration now cover households, rooms, caregivers, hub/nodes, events, routines/windows, alerts, acknowledgements, notification jobs, histories, configuration and audit. The connected simulator intentionally still uses InMemoryStore; flash adapters, DB repository wiring, journal compaction and retained-event refill are not closed.
Acceptance experiment: Test full capacity, interruption at each commit step, reboot before ACK, compaction and offline retention exhaustion. Require an explicit gap/fault outcome when evidence cannot be retained.

Boundary: Trusted/untrusted time and boundary suppression are covered by the pure rule engine and connected scenarios. Production authenticated time acquisition, reboot checkpoints, timezone/DST handling and range/overflow validation remain target work.
Acceptance experiment: Test missing anchor, stale anchor, clock rollback, uncertainty straddling a boundary and daylight-saving dates for non-India homes. Keep absolute timestamps and elapsed timer tests separate.

Boundary: Household settings are schema-validated, versioned through GET/POST config APIs and applied to HomeConfig/activity rules; stale versions are rejected. Durable authenticated command envelopes and crash-safe target-side application remain deployment/HIL work.
Acceptance experiment: Reorder versions, duplicate the newest, corrupt one field and power-cycle during application. Verify that the active snapshot is entirely old or entirely new.

Browser/manual: Access behavior covered by HTTP tests
Boundary: Tenant-scope, unknown-actor and cross-origin negative tests exist, and consent-aware state is represented. Production TLS/OIDC, device key management, secure boot, credential rotation and mutation-role policy are not established by the host lab.
Acceptance experiment: Run cross-tenant read/write, revoked credential, wrong session and invalid signature cases. Inspect the deployed endpoints and logs; do not infer security from class names or a mock signature verifier.

Boundary: Manifest/wrong-board/rollback policy is unit-tested through a host seam. Actual image download, cryptographic signature/hash verification, flash partitions, bootloader rollback and watchdog recovery require target-board evidence.
Acceptance experiment: Test wrong board, stale version, bad hash text and rejected signature on host. Later interrupt download/write/first boot on hardware and demonstrate recovery before a field update.

Boundary: v1.5.4 adds a fail-closed release framework: 24/24 P0 mappings, 4 contract schemas, 80 C++ checks, 24 Python tests, 10 JS tests, 4/4 feature variants, Base/AI profile checks, 5/5 dummy streams, 68/68 functional scenarios, 16/16 HTTP tests, ASan/UBSan and trace-build passes. Browser automation remains manual-required in this environment; hardware/pilot acceptance remains separate.
Acceptance experiment: Inject queue exhaustion, provider failure and missing sink; verify error records without secrets. Run TRACE-on/off profiles and separate sanitizer and target crash-recovery tests. Record toolchain, command, result and remaining limitations.

Boundary: Build-selected product identity and invalid-product handling remain host-validated in the release gate. This does not imply future AI capabilities are product-complete.
Acceptance experiment: make verify PRODUCT=base|ai; invalid PRODUCT fails; Product::name/version identify build.

Boundary: tests/cpp/test_product.cpp: base branch
Acceptance experiment: Base begin returns Disabled and fake provider receives zero starts.

Boundary: Controller tests pass; consent propagation and audio capture gate pending
Acceptance experiment: Reject missing consent/offline before start; active session rejects a second start.

Boundary: tests/cpp/test_product.cpp: timeout and completion checks
Acceptance experiment: Reject wrong, duplicate and late IDs; expire at 30000 monotonic milliseconds.

Boundary: Controller cancellation tested; physical and privacy wiring pending
Acceptance experiment: Controller cancels pending provider; physical cancel and consent withdrawal stop recording/playback.

Boundary: Coordinator and load/latency tests not implemented
Acceptance experiment: Monitoring never waits for model response; urgent prompt preempts interaction.

Boundary: No live provider, microphone capture or speech synthesis implemented
Acceptance experiment: Bounded audio buffers; authenticated provider path; explain offline/unavailable state.

Boundary: No capability endpoint or spending limiter implemented
Acceptance experiment: Server enforces tenant/edition/consent/quota; UI reflects availability, not authorization.

Boundary: Metadata-only hooks exist; live adapter and incident-isolation integration tests pending
Acceptance experiment: Controller logs no audio/transcript; AI response cannot acknowledge or resolve incidents.

Boundary: Host rules and UI semantics avoid converting activity/no-activity into medical wellbeing conclusions. Field/user comprehension and commercial claims review remain outside host evidence.
Acceptance experiment: No fall, medical, emergency-dispatch or wellbeing claim from P0 evidence.

Boundary: Dashboard age/presentation and local semantic feedback paths are host-tested, but the <500 ms physical button-feedback target must be measured on real hub/button/display hardware.
Acceptance experiment: Local valid button confirmation within 500 ms; dashboard displays data age.

Boundary: Host WAN-loss and replay behavior is regression-tested without duplicate backend ingestion. Real flash retention, router power, RF loss and outage-duration endurance remain HIL/pilot items.
Acceptance experiment: Local operation during WAN outage; recovery replays unsent events without duplication.

Boundary: Bounded host queues, callback separation and sanitizer tests provide software evidence. Exact FreeRTOS scheduling, queue saturation and CPU/stack behavior on the selected boards are still unmeasured.
Acceptance experiment: State-owner queues are bounded; no unbounded retry or blocking work in radio callback.

Boundary: ASan/UBSan, bounded host logging and schema/storage limits are tested. Actual ESP32 RAM/stack/flash/current/runtime/thermal measurements remain mandatory before pilot.
Acceptance experiment: Measure RAM/flash/CPU/battery on actual ESP32 hardware; fail release if agreed budgets are exceeded.

Boundary: Host tenant isolation, credential/update policy seams and negative API behavior are tested. This is not penetration testing and does not establish production TLS/OIDC, ESP-NOW crypto, secure boot or secret storage.
Acceptance experiment: Unique credentials, encrypted/authenticated transport, signed OTA and least-privilege access.

Boundary: P0 remains camera-free/no always-on listening; consent withdrawal enters the internal privacy state and normal Settings no longer exposes a generic privacy toggle. Real data-lifecycle enforcement and field privacy review remain pending.
Acceptance experiment: Camera-free/no always-on listening P0; consent withdrawal is effective and auditable.

Boundary: Versioned contracts, deterministic rules, a canonical 68-case catalog, requirement-coverage mapping and reproducible release commands are now formalized. Source traceability metadata still needs periodic synchronization as code evolves.
Acceptance experiment: Module IDs, contracts, deterministic rules, automated tests and reproducible builds.

Boundary: ERROR/TRACE profiles, log analyzer and simulated diagnostic codes are host-tested. Target flash wear, concurrent FreeRTOS writes, brownout/watchdog/panic and coredump retrieval require hardware evidence.
Acceptance experiment: Bounded structured `.txt` diagnostics; ERROR always; TRACE build-gated; no secrets.

Boundary: Large-action/clear-label and non-color-only design intent is represented in the UI/manual checklist. Actual target-device accessibility and resident/caregiver comprehension testing are still required.
Acceptance experiment: Large resident actions, clear labels, visible local state and caregiver-readable uncertainty.
